# MultiSQL: A Schema-Integrated Context-Dependent Text2SQL Dataset with Diverse SQL Operations

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#multisql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-acl.823.pdf) · Findings of ACL 2024 proceedings, pages 13857-13867

**Reading coverage:** All eleven PDF pages, Sections 1-8, limitations and Appendix A; Tables 1-6 and all figure descriptions/examples covered.

## Research question

Read-only conversational SQL benchmarks miss dialogue-driven changes to database contents and schema.

## Method

GPT-4 extends CoSQL-derived interactions with SELECT and mutation/schema operations. Human correction removes errors and adds contextual dependencies. The prompt baseline supplies dialogue history and optional executor feedback for self-refinement.

## Evaluation

The final corpus contains 783 dialogues and 9,257 turns over 166 databases. Llama tuning uses 662 dialogues, with 121 reserved for testing. Metrics include SELECT execution accuracy, heuristic name-mapped context-aware matching and database-state matching for mutations.

## What the results support

History and refinement improve several GPT-4 results, including SELECT execution accuracy, but gains are not uniform across operations or weaker models. Long dialogue and schema changes remain difficult.

## Limits and qualifications

The dialogue corpus is synthesized and manually refined rather than sampled live user interaction. Appendix A uses GPT-3.5 to extract SQL from Llama outputs, so those results include postprocessing assistance. Fuzzy identifier matching and instance-state comparisons do not establish unrestricted semantic equivalence. Explicit clarification and unanswerability policies are not evaluated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful for testing state tracking and error propagation in database agents, separately from recognizing ambiguity.
